neighbours.label: structural parts of geometric or graph objects (faces, nodes, edges, centre) in math or code
fire: A cube has six square faces, twelve edges and eight vertices.
In a binary tree every interior node has exactly two children.
The Delaunay triangulation connects each point to its nearest neighbours.
Two adjacent faces of the polyhedron share a common edge.
The algorithm visits each node of the graph once and marks its edges.
The centroid of the triangle lies inside, two thirds of the way along each median.
A planar graph can be drawn so that no two edges are crossing.
Each leaf node stores a pointer to its parent node in the tree.
quiet: A cube of sugar dissolves quickly in a cup of hot tea.
In a big family every child has exactly two parents.
The new road connects each village to its nearest market town.
Two neighbours on the street share a common garden fence.
The postman visits each house on the street once a day.
The town centre lies a short walk from the railway station.
A careful driver slows down near busy pedestrian crossings.
Each autumn the leaves fall from the tall trees in the park.

notes: Card: gate-closed echo dominates (92%); peaks on ' center', ' node', ' face', Delaunay, non-crossing. Probe: 'six faces and twelve edges' 0.52, 'interior node' 0.50. Near misses use the same words in everyday senses or plain math without structure words.
